newsitem.title: GERMANY: Six people held captive in German bank.
newsitem.headline: Six people held captive in German bank.

text.p: A holdup man took six people hostage at a bank in southwest Germany on Friday and threatened to shoot them unless he gets five million marks ($3 million) and a getaway car.
Local prosecutors said they believed the man had tried to rob the bank in the town of Neuenstein, near Heidelberg, but grabbed the hostages when his plan went awry.
Prosecutor Roland Kleinschroth said the man was demanding the money be paid in 100 and 200 mark notes.
His deadline for police to meet his demands passed at 10 p.m. local time (2000 GMT) without reporters near the bank hearing or seeing anything out of the ordinary.

Kleinschroth said the man appeared to accept that police needed more time to get the money together. "It's the money he's interested in," Kleinschroth told reporters at a makeshift news conference close to the scene.
The man seized the hostages in the late afternoon and has threatened to shoot hostages if anyone goes near the building, police said.
"We're in regular contact with him," police spokesman Juergen Merwald told reprters. "Normally he calls the police but he's also calling various television and radio stations."
One local radio station said he had telephoned its office three times. He said one hostage would be shot every hour if police did not respect his deadline, Radio Regenbogen reported.
In the third call, a loud bang could be heard after an interviewer asked him what weapons he had. The caller said he had not shot anyone but was just proving he was armed.
He said he was holding four bank employees, a cleaner and a customer.
Police sealed off the area around the bank and asked nearby residents not to leave their homes.
Kleinschroth said experts analysing the man's voice believed he was about 30 years old.
